1

Details

The question (Sept 2026): same-chamber coincident pairs came out of the reconstruction badly or not at all. What is the best that could be done in principle (a toy), how far is the reconstruction from it, and what explains the difference?

Three limits are compared throughout. The physical limit is what a perfect analysis could resolve if the forward model were exact: about one strip pitch. The real-track limit is the same ideal fit on real tracks, where the forward model is imperfect: about 2–3 mm. Production is the current wft.reco chain, which was far from both.

The fixed chain is four opt-in switches: WFT_TWO_TRACK_SCALE=two, WFT_TWO_TRACK_SEARCH=grid, no trigger, and every candidate tried. Profile pairing is the x/y pairing calibration xy_pairing_*_profc.json. With all switches off, output is production’s, bit for bit.

How the note runs: where it started and how the work unfolded (slides 2–4); the problem and the first truth bench (5–7); the limit ladder: toy, synthetic planes, real overlays (8–12); the fixed chain, its progression, the contract and the operating threshold (13–16); x/y pairing; the relative angle of the pairs; then the single-track thread (in-situ bundle, seeder, beam angle scale) and what has to ride the one re-pass.

Decided: the operating threshold, A F = 1200 and C F = 2400 (real-trigger rescan, condor cluster 4348153). Explained (7 Oct pm): the beam/cosmic angle-scale gap is electron scattering between the gap and the wall (Geant4), so the cosmic in-situ scale is the angle truth. Not decided: shipping, which now waits on the new bundles and on adopting that scale for beam.

It started in the data: a second track in the chamber spoils both, and close pairs vanish

Campaign stage-3 tracks (33 runs), gated, pointing at the capsule. intra_vertex, 2026-09-13.

chamber A

chamber C

intra_multiplicity.csv, intra_twotrack_separation.csv. Hover a bar or point for n, strips and χ²/dof.

2

Details

Same-chamber pairs (A–A, C–C, D–D) are about a third of the two-track sample, 19 707 of ~62 700 real pairs at the published 30 mm cut. They are the only pairs where both legs are measured by one chamber on one calibration, so the natural place to test whether two tracks share a vertex, and where small-opening-angle backgrounds (conversions, low-angle IPC) live. In September all three event-mixed vertex tests on them came out blind.

Left: a track that shares its chamber with another is measured 3–4× worse in y at the capsule, its fit takes 2–3× the strips at 6–10× the χ²/dof. Right: of 25,292 tracks in two-track A chambers, 1 has its partner within 12 mm in y. Close pairs are not reconstructed as two tracks at all. On the detector-A intra control, 0 real intra-A pairs below 20 mm (and 56 below 40 mm) were seen, where event mixing expects ~12 400.

The damage also grew with separation (A y: 79 mm at 16–24 mm, 142–146 mm beyond 24 mm), which is not what overlapping charge does. Four hypotheses followed (HANDOFF_INTRA_TWO_TRACK_RECO §4): H1 x/y swaps of time-degenerate tracks, H2a merging under the seed gap, H2b windows spanning both tracks, H3 two-track events are intrinsically messier. Only a truth sample separates them, which is why the overlay bench was built.

Source: ntof_athens_26/pair_vertex_imaging/intra_vertex.py --multiplicity → <out>/pair_vertex/intra_multiplicity.csv, intra_twotrack_separation.csv.

+45/52/40 % scintillator-confirmed tracks; in-situ A closes on cosmics; walls give D_eff ≈ 330 mm. Beam vs cosmic gap open.

10-07

Beam/cosmic gap explained: electron scattering

Cosmics read 1.15 at A’s wall (= the A–C line); in-beam muons read like beam-off ones. Geant4, ideal reco: the wall estimator reads 0.59 on beam electrons, 1.00 on muons. The cosmic scale stands.

The starting question, Sept 2026: what is the best that can be done in principle, how far is the reconstruction from it, and what explains the difference? T1 answered it for the two-track step. The answer turned out to rest on the single-track reconstruction underneath, which T2 now tests against cosmic truth.

3

Details

The study began as one question about same-chamber coincident pairs: what is the best that could be done in principle, how far is the reconstruction from it, and what explains the difference? The first two weeks answered that for the two-track step itself (T1). That answer turned out to rest on things outside the two-track step: the single-track angle calibration, the seeder, and the depth profile of late tracks. Those became separate threads (T2 on the beam-off-cosmics branch, T3 late tracks) that now constrain T1.

4

Details

This is the map of the note. Left to right is the order in which an event is reconstructed (wft, then stage 3). Rows: what production does today, what this study measured it to cost, and the opt-in replacement.

Nothing here is in production. Every fix is behind a switch that, when off, reproduces production output bit for bit. They are meant to ride a single campaign re-pass together (last slides), after one combined validation.

The first four stages are T1 and T2’s fixes; the last two are why the broadened scope matters: a two-track efficiency is not useful if the depth profile of a late track is unconstrained, and an opening angle is only as good as the angle scale under it. That scale is now understood (the cosmic in-situ scale is the truth; the beam walls read electron scattering) but not yet adopted.

Two tracks in one plane share strips; the reconstruction must decide to split

A one-track fit is always made. A two-track fit replaces it only past a threshold.

The question: at what separation can two tracks in one readout plane be told apart, and how far is the reconstruction from that?

Fit one track

forward model: line + t0 + depth-charge profile

→

Trigger?

attempt a split only if residuals look like a second track

Fit two tracks

seeded from the parent fit

→

fstat ≥ F?

and the 1.2 mm guard passes

Three limits throughout: physical (perfect model, ideal fit) · real-track (ideal fit on real windows) · production (what we run). Hover the dotted terms and chart points for definitions and counts.

5

Details

Each readout plane (x or y view) of a micro-TPC chamber sees a track as a line in (strip, drift time). Two tracks in the same plane share strips wherever they are closer than a few pitches, and the resistive layer spreads each strip's charge to its neighbours, so their signals overlap.

Reconstruction (wft.reco) fits one track to every window. A trigger (a residual z-score probe) decides whether to try a split; the two-track fit is then accepted when its improvement fstat clears the threshold TWO_TRACK_F (300 in production, 120 when the other view already sees two tracks), and a distinguishability guard refuses children closer than 1.2 mm.

Two populations matter: real pairs (which we want to split) and single tracks (which we must not split). Every threshold trades one against the other, so every comparison in this note is made at a matched rate of false splits on real single tracks.

6

Details

The bench (2026-09-14, intra_bench.py) overlays the decoded waveforms of two clean single-track triggers of the same chamber, file tag and trigger phase, then reconstructs the overlay with the production chain and compares against each donor’s own fit. Pairs are coincident (|Δt0| < 30 ns), offset, or between. The harness reproduces production’s fits bit for bit on the donors themselves.

What it found, against the four hypotheses of the previous slide:

  1. H1 x/y swaps, confirmed. When both tracks are prompt, select_tracks pairs the strongest x with the strongest y. Wrong in ~75 % of cases where the views rank the tracks differently.
  2. H2a merging, confirmed. Below 12 mm the seed clusterer makes one window, so at most one track.
  3. A mechanism not on the list: the seed significance floor is 10 % of the brightest strip of the whole plane, so a bright partner anywhere erases a fainter track (~16 % of tracks at ≥ 24 mm).
  4. H2b not reproduced: found tracks fit like singles. The data’s widened fits come from busier real events (H3).

The categories overlap (a pair can have one track swapped and the other seed-lost), so the bars do not sum to 100 %. This is the first bench, on --overlay add; see the next slide for why its ≥ 24 mm numbers are pessimistic.

Source: <out>/intra_bench/compare.csv, variant production. Record: wft/MULTITRACK_2026-09-14.md, handoff §10.

7

Details

The first bench summed donor b’s whole waveforms onto donor a’s over b’s region, so b’s strips carried two triggers’ noise. The fit is not told, and telling it (σ×√2) does not help. Measured directly by adding an empty trigger’s waveforms on a clean donor’s own region, with no second track (scratch selfnoise.py, numbers in TWO_TRACK_FIT_LOG.md 2026-09-29).

Fix (bench only, opt-in): build --overlay replace: on b’s region outside a’s, b’s waveforms replace a’s. Only strips both regions share still carry two triggers’ noise, which is unavoidable there.

Consequences: every overlay number before 09-29 was low at ≥ 12 mm (below 12 mm the regions overlap anyway). What was left at ≥ 24 mm was x/y pairing (11.7 / 7.2 % swapped donor tracks, A / C), not a “flat algorithmic plateau”. And t0 is fragile at the one-sample level on real noise, so the ±120 ns x/y gate has little margin, in real events too.

The information limit: about one strip pitch

Noise-free forward-model pairs, 1 450 ADC·bin each, scored at the run’s noise (13.3 ADC).

A, tan 0

A, tan 0.3

C, tan 0

C, tan 0.3

λ collapses like ~d⁴ near zero and saturates once the tracks stop overlapping.

Vertical tracks cross the threshold at ~0.75 mm, about one strip pitch. An inclined track (tan 0.3) spreads each depth slice over fewer strips per unit charge, so the same d carries ~50× less information: ~1.5 mm.

This is the physical limit. Nothing below assumes it can be beaten.

R1 · r1_asimov.csv. Hover any point for λ and the peak signal-to-noise.

8

Details

Two tracks with the same slope and t0 are generated noise-free by the forward model under the run_145 bundle, with a flat depth profile to 840 ns. The best single track is fitted to that window; the χ² it leaves is λ, the Δχ² a perfect analysis expects between one and two tracks (its Asimov value).

Chamber C’s tan 0 curve flattens between 0.5 and 1 mm because C’s bundle puts a vertical track on one strip (σp0 = 0.039 mm, not revalidated): its tan 0 numbers are the model’s, not the chamber’s. No clean real donor has |tan θ| < 0.05 anyway.

Source: two_track_limit.py asimov → r1_asimov.csv.

Production loses pairs the ideal fit resolves

9

Details

The ideal fit (pure χ², one- and two-track fits from the truth and from a broad start set, threshold at the 99th percentile of Δχ² on 400 synthetic singles) is run against production’s own fit, probe, trigger and joint fit on the same planes (same seeds), cut to a production window.

Production’s losses are algorithmic, each one measured:

  1. The trigger fires on ~0 % of tan 0.3 pairs below 12 mm (and on none of A’s vertical pairs at 2–4 mm).
  2. The fstat scale. scale = χ²_one/dof contains the second track’s unexplained charge, so fstat ≈ λ/(1+λ/dof) < dof ≈ 200–300 < F = 300 for a close vertical pair. Fix: WFT_TWO_TRACK_SCALE=two takes the scale from the two-track fit.
  3. The search. Children seeded from the one-track parent settle into an “X”. Every unfound case had a lower-χ² true solution (27/27). Fix: WFT_TWO_TRACK_SEARCH=grid, a global grid of parallel line pairs then Nelder–Mead: 96–100 %, median χ² gap to truth 0.
  4. The 1.2 mm guard is a hard floor where the ideal is already 77–100 %. It was kept: on real singles it blocks 42 % of false splits.

False splits on synthetic singles are 0–2 % for every chain, identical with and without the fixes.

Source: two_track_limit.py oracle / synthprod → r4_synth_ladder.csv.

Real tracks are not their perfect-model twins: the threshold rises ×19–24

Δχ² gained by splitting well-modelled single tracks (χ²/dof < 2), ideal fit.

Each real single track is refitted with the ideal two-track fit, and so is its perfect-model twin. The twin’s split gains what noise gives; the real track also gains whatever the forward model fails to describe.

So the threshold that keeps false splits at 1 % rises ×19 in A and ×24 in C, and the mismatch grows with the track’s charge.

That is why real tracks resolve from ~2–3 mm, not one pitch: the model, not the information, sets the real limit.

Bar: 99th percentile (the threshold). Black tick: median.

R3 · r3_null.csv. 600 single donors per (chamber, view) before the χ²/dof cut.

10

Details

The windows are 61 strips wide, so some hold charge the donor does not explain (another cluster, saturation). A window counts as well modelled when its donor, refitted alone on it, reaches χ²/dof < 2: A 87 % of singles, C 55 %. On all windows the thresholds are set by that foreign charge instead, and the real ideal fit collapses (see the next slide’s Details).

Two things were tried to close the gap and dropped: a fractional model error ε in the χ² (no gain at a fixed false-split rate), and a looser guard (it blocks 42 % of false splits on real singles).

Details

Worker options for a condor job (as in make_two_track_package.py): TWO_TRACK_SCALE=two, TWO_TRACK_SEARCH=grid, TWO_TRACK_RESID_Z=-inf, TWO_TRACK_MAX_TRY=99, TWO_TRACK_SELECTED_ONLY=false, TWO_TRACK_F and TWO_TRACK_F_CORROB = 0.4 F.

14

Details

Each point is the same set of coincident overlays (run_145 stat090_0000, stratified by separation; hover for k/n) reconstructed with one more change. Separation is the smaller of the x and y mesh separations.

  1. + pairing + rescue floor (09-14): x/y pairing by charge for time-degenerate tracks; a local significance floor that adds clusters the plane-wide floor erased, ranked below production’s. Lifts ≥ 24 mm; nothing below 12 mm, where one window holds both.
  2. + joint fit (09-16): a two-track fit inside one window, at production’s F = 300 / 120 with its trigger. The first pairs below 12 mm.
  3. Bench fix (09-29, grey column): the overlay stopped doubling the noise. Same reconstruction.
  4. Fixed chain (09-30): no trigger, every candidate, grid search, two-track noise scale, at F matched to production’s false-split rate (A 1200, C 2400).
  5. + profile pairing: the x/y cost gains a constrained depth-profile term (xy_pairing_*_profc.json).

C is held back below 12 mm by its stricter threshold: the overlay scan says C resolves 58 % at F = 2400, 69 % at 1200. The real-trigger rescan says F = 2400 is nonetheless the lowest that meets the contract (Operating point). Parallel, co-located tracks are degenerate at any Δt and stay lost.

Variants: production (bench root), pairing_rescue16_ranked, pairing_rescue16_two_final, …_replace, fixed_{A,C}_replace, fixed_{A,C}_replace_profc under <out>/intra_bench/. The first three are on --overlay add.

15

Details

Real triggers are re-reconstructed with each chain and matched to the frozen full pass, on the same triggers for both chains, both with x/y re-pairing (which alone moves ~5 % of unsplit events against the frozen pass, which was reconstructed without it).

The contract is clean single muons split ≤ 0.66 % (production’s own rate on C) and no event losing a track. The sample is small: 0.66 % of C’s 1 057 clean singles is 7 events, so neighbouring thresholds are not statistically distinct.

C’s fixed chain at F = 2400 splits far fewer real events than production (207 vs 913) and recovers twice as many of production’s own tracks: inside the contract with room to spare. The F rescan measured that room: one step lower (F = 2000) already fails. Real triggers have no truth: split-ab bounds the cost of a threshold, while the gain comes only from the overlay bench.

Real triggers confirm the matched thresholds

Lowest F meeting the contract on real triggers: A F = 1200, C F = 2400. Bench curves for the gain.

bench: pairs resolved

bench: single donors split

real triggers: clean singles split

Is C’s threshold too strict? No: the bench-matched F is already the lowest that meets the contract. A at F = 1000 splits 0.83 % of clean singles (bench pairs 66 → 68 %); C at F = 2000 splits 0.76 % of clean singles (bench pairs 58 → 61 %), both over 0.66 %. Picked by point estimate; neighbouring F values are not statistically distinct.

16

Details

Sources: bench, r3_scan.parquet (fixed_f0); real triggers, split_ab_ladder_{A,C}_7tags/summary_ladder.csv.

Bench donors split more readily than clean singles on real triggers (C at 2400: 1.2 % vs 0.47 %). The matched thresholds were set on the bench, so they may be stricter than the real data needs, and the real-trigger rescan, not the bench, should set F.

How one pass covers every threshold: neither the split attempts nor their fstat depend on F, only acceptance does. wft.reco.two_track_ladder keeps both children of every attempt and, for each F, rebuilds the candidate lists, applies the worker’s lost-track revert and runs the selector. The replay was verified exact, event by event, against primary runs at F = 2400 and 300 before submission.

Check before believing it: each chamber’s ladder row at its matched F must reproduce split_ab_fixed_<arm>_7tags/summary.csv (events split, gaining a track, not recovered).

constrained charge

+ depth profile

Two prompt tracks give two x and two y candidates, and timing cannot tell which x goes with which y. Both views see the same drifting charge, so each track’s depth profile q(t) should match across views.

Compared bin by bin in each view’s own t0 frame, profiles fail (72 / 80 %): t0 slides by whole bins between views. On a common absolute-time grid they carry real information.

The floor for C: some tracks disagree with themselves across views (x/y charge 2069/515). No pairing built on shared charge can place them.

Open: the 3-strip seeder re-pairs 5–13 % of production’s tracks in busy events. Validate it together with this pairing.

TWO_TRACK_FIT_LOG 2026-09-30 (scratch profile_pairing.py): A 2 437, C 695 coincident donor pairs.

17

Details

Decision: for two coincident clean donors, keep or swap the y partners; the lower summed cost wins. Production’s cost is the x/y charge ratio (lq) plus time. The constrained versions zero the depth bins the window cannot see before summing (wft.reco.constrained_charge, feature lqc), because on 12–33 % of stage-3 tracks per view those bins hold runaway charge (q_sum > 10⁶) and the charge ratio saturates. The profile term is the distance between the two views’ constrained, normalised profiles on an absolute-time grid, smoothed by 1–2 bins.

Held-out numbers (calibrated on stat090_0001, tested on 0000; TWO_TRACK_FIT_LOG.md 2026-09-30). On the event-level bench at ≥ 24 mm, A’s swapped donor tracks fall 12.2 → 7.2 % and efficiency rises 85 → 91 %; C barely moves, for the reason in the callout.

The x/y charge ratio is flat with position (median log ratio within ±0.05 across the chamber), so a gain map would not help. Its per-track spread is 0.48 (A) / 0.67 (C) on all gated tracks against 0.12–0.20 on clean donors.

Not done: a joint x–y fit with each track’s profile shared between views (handoff §1.3), the only idea that adds information rather than a better cost.

A common vertex makes close pairs parallel

Relative angle and separation are one variable for a pair from the capsule.

Two legs of one vertex are straight lines from the same point. Their angle inside the chamber is the opening angle, and it fixes their separation: d ≈ Lθ. Across the drift gap the separation changes by only 13 %.

separation dθ = d / Ldivergence over 30 mm
1 mm0.24°0.13 mm
3 mm0.73°0.38 mm
6 mm1.47°0.77 mm
12 mm2.93°1.53 mm
24 mm5.86°3.07 mm
50 mm12.21°6.39 mm

So for a common-vertex pair, “close” and “parallel” are the same thing. A sharp angle between close tracks needs two vertices: an unrelated pair.

18

Details

The question this section answers: the bench bins pairs by separation, but two tracks at a sharp relative angle should be much easier to split than two parallel ones. What angle do the modelled pairs have, how much does angle help, and what angle do real pairs have?

Geometry first. A pair from one vertex at distance L from the strip plane, with opening angle θ, lands d ≈ Lθ apart. Both legs are straight, so their relative angle inside the chamber is θ too. Over the 30 mm gap, which is nearer the source, the separation shrinks by a factor (L − 30)/L. The change is 12.8 % of d: 1.5 mm at 12 mm, 0.4 mm at 3 mm.

Off-centre vertices change this little. The capsule is 10 mm in radius, so in the x view a vertex shifts the pointing by at most ±10 mm out of 235. Along the beam (y view) the capsule is 80 mm long, but both legs of one pair share the vertex, so its position does not enter their relative angle.

Not modelled: multiple scattering between the vertex and the chamber. Scattering in the capsule wall changes the opening angle, but the scattered legs still come from (nearly) one point, so d ≈ Lθ still holds. Only scattering close to the chamber (window, gas) breaks it.

Angle does help: a 2 mm divergence resolves pairs that touch at the strips

Perfect forward model, ideal fit, white noise at 13.3 ADC, view x, tan 0.3. Track b diverges from a by D over the drift column. 40 pairs per point; threshold at 1 % false splits.

diverging 0 mm

diverging 0.5 mm

diverging 1 mm

diverging 2 mm

diverging 4 mm

diverging 8 mm

crossing

R5 · pair_angle.py. Hover a point for k/n, the r.m.s. separation and the noise-free Δχ².

19

Details

This is R2’s oracle with one change: the second track is tilted relative to the first. Its slope differs by D / 840 ns, so the two lines separate by D more at the far end of the 840 ns column than at the strips. D = −2d is a symmetric crossing at mid-column. Truth is known, the fitter is ideal (one- and two-track fits from the truth and from a broad start set), and the threshold is R2’s own 99th percentile of Δχ² on 400 synthetic singles at tan 0.3 (view x), so this ladder sits on R2’s and is directly comparable.

Parallel pairs (D = 0) reproduce R2: A 25 %, C 35 % at 0.5 mm. Divergence adds information at every separation. Its effect is largest where the pair touches at the strips. Above ~2 mm everything is resolved anyway.

Noise-free Δχ² (hover a point): at d = 0, λ grows from ~3 (D = 1 mm) to ~40–60 (2 mm) and ~250–330 (4 mm). The 1 % threshold is ~25.

The catch is the green line. A common-vertex pair diverges by only 13 % of its separation, so on this axis it lives on the parallel curve. The angle carries a lot of information, but the pairs we want do not have much of it.

Source: pair_angle.py asimov, oracle --n 40 → r5_asimov.csv, r5_oracle.parquet.

Tracks point at the capsule: slope is tied to position in x, loosely in y

The bench’s donors: clean single tracks, run_145 stat090_0000, both slopes measured, pointing within 30 mm of the beam axis.

chamber A

chamber C

fitted pointing line

intra_bench donors.parquet · pair_angle.py data → pointing.csv. Robust σ = half the 16–84 % range.

20

Details

Every donor of the overlay bench is shown, in the model’s own units (the fitted tan θ = w / v that the forward model uses, before the per-arm angle scale k). The line is a straight-line fit of tan θ against position. Its slope is 1/Leff: A x 1/294 mm, C x 1/387 mm. That is flatter than the geometric 1/235 mm because fitted slopes are compressed by charge sharing (the angle scale k, CLAUDE.md and campaign_angle).

x view: scatter ±0.054 (A), ±0.040 (C). That is about the single-track slope resolution, plus at most ±10 mm/235 from the capsule radius. The slope is essentially fixed by the position.

y view: scatter ±0.14 (A), ±0.13 (C), four times wider. The pointing cut is a distance to the beam axis, so along the beam the vertex is free: the 80 mm capsule and anything else on the axis. Two donors from different triggers at the same y position can therefore differ in slope by ~0.2–0.3.

That matters for the next slide. The bench pairs donors from different triggers, so their vertices differ. A real pair shares one vertex.

Bench pairs diverge more than a common-vertex pair would

Real-overlay pairs (R3, well-modelled windows), divergence from the two donors’ fitted slopes.

divergence < 1 mm

1–3 mm

≥ 3 mm

At event level, 80 % of coincident bench overlays closer than 12 mm have a view diverging by ≥ 3 mm, mostly y. A pair from one vertex diverges by ≤ 1.5 mm there.

21

Details

Left: every per-view pair of the R3 real-overlay bench in chamber A, at its separation at the strips, with the divergence 30 mm × |Δtan θ| from the two donors’ own fits. The green line is where a pair from one vertex would sit (30/L = 0.128 × d). x-view pairs (blue) scatter about it within the slope-error floor. y-view pairs (purple) spread far above it, because the two donors come from different points along the beam.

Right: the same pairs, resolved or not, split by divergence. Pairs that touch at the strips (< 1 mm) are resolved by the ideal fit 24 % (42) when parallel and 90 % (31) when diverging ≥ 3 mm (n in brackets). The data says the same as the oracle: angle helps exactly where separation fails. A common-vertex pair is in the parallel class, so below ~3 mm the bench average is optimistic for genuine pairs; above 3 mm the classes agree.

A side finding about the fixed chain. At 3–12 mm it resolves 93 % (102) of parallel pairs but only 76 % (91) of strongly diverging ones, where the ideal fit gets 97 % (91). The loss is in the y view. The cause is plausibly the grid search, which seeds parallel line pairs (a common tan); a relative-tan dimension in the grid is the obvious fix. It matters for unrelated pairs, not for common-vertex ones.

Caveat: each divergence is estimated from two fitted slopes, with an r.m.s. error of about 1.9 mm, so the < 1 mm and 1–3 mm classes mix. The ≥ 3 mm class is mostly genuinely diverging.

Real pairs in chamber A are unrelated tracks at wide angles

Every pair of gated tracks in one chamber-A trigger, all post-access production runs (296,218 pairs), against pairs mixed across triggers.

same trigger

mixed across triggers (no shared vertex)

common vertex, θ = d / L

det_a_intra pairs.parquet (production chain, chamber A) · pair_angle.py data. Right panel thinned to 1 500 pairs per sample.

22

Details

Source: det_a_intra, which pairs every gated, angle-calibrated chamber-A track within a trigger, with a cross-trigger mixed sample as the geometric null (no shared vertex possible). The angles are the production chain’s, from waveforms.

Same-trigger pairs look like mixed pairs. They have the same separation distribution and the same opening angles at every separation: median 31° for all pairs, against 32° mixed. Among pairs with both slopes measured, 49° against 47°. Only 0.068 % of same-trigger pairs vertex near the axis, against 0.074 % of mixed ones. So the two-track sample is dominated by two unrelated particles in one trigger. The intuition that pairs are rarely parallel holds for them: they are far from it.

No real pair closer than 24 mm survives production (0 of 296,218), where mixing predicts 1.6 %. That is the production loss this whole study is about. The data therefore cannot show the angle of close real pairs; it can only show what the population is made of.

Pointing pairs (right) follow the common-vertex line only loosely. The pointing cut is a distance to the beam axis (≤ 30 mm), so a pair can “point” from two different places along the beam. That is the same y-view freedom as on the pointing slide.

Genuine pairs are rarely close: 5 % of same-chamber M1 pairs are within 12 mm

Expected IPC opening-angle law through a point-source toy of the four strip planes.

M1 (the measured 55 μb channel)

E0 (no real photon)

Where would a genuine pair land? The IPC continuum from ipc_born (the expected spectrum, CLAUDE.md), thrown from the capsule centre with an isotropic pair axis. Both legs must cross one strip plane.

in one chamber< 6 mm< 12 mm< 24 mm
M127 %1.4 %5.2 %16.5 %
E010 %0.1 %0.4 %1.6 %

Same-chamber IPC pairs are mostly well separated: only 5 % (M1) are closer than 12 mm. Those few are parallel, and those are the ones the bench average flatters.

Prior, not a measurement: ipc_born (M1, E0) through pair_angle.ipc_toy. Hover the curves for cumulative fractions.

23

Details

This is a prior, not data. For the two s-wave channels open after the flash veto, ipc_born.sample('M1') and e0_lab() give the opening-angle law with its weights. Leg 1 is thrown isotropically and leg 2 at the opening angle with a random azimuth, from the centre of the capsule. A pair counts as same-chamber when both legs cross the same 380 × 340 mm strip plane at L = 235 mm. Pinwheel offsets, dead strips, capsule size and efficiency are ignored.

The X17 itself never lands in one chamber: at 20.6 MeV its opening angle is at least 2 asin(m/E) ≈ 110°, against ~90° for the largest pair one plane can hold.

What the toy leaves out and the real sample may have: external conversions of the 20.6 MeV M1 photon in the capsule wall or the chamber window. Those pairs are extremely collimated (θ ~ me/E, a few mm apart) and exactly parallel. If they matter for an analysis, they live in the hardest corner of this study.

Source: pair_angle.py data → ipc_intra_sep.csv, ipc_intra_sep_fine.csv.

Two tracks need two right single tracks: the question split into three threads

What each thread asks and has established, and how they constrain each other. Hover a link.

24

Details

The goal is unchanged: reconstruct two tracks from one vertex in one chamber, with correct angles. T1 answered “can we separate them”. Doing so showed it rests on the single-track reconstruction, which T2 tests against an independent truth: a cosmic muon crossing chambers A and C is one straight line, so each chamber’s own track must lie along the line joining the two (run_149, 87 sub-runs, 1.9 M triggers, beam off).

The two branches share no code; they meet in the seeder and the calibration bundles. Map: sept26_prelim_analysis/SAME_CHAMBER_PAIRS.md (identical on both branches).

On cosmic truth the in-situ bundle reads true angles; production’s were shallow

run_149 beam-off through-goers, held-out third (truth = line joining chambers A and C, 469 mm lever). Seeder 3 for both.

A, production bundle

A, in-situ bundle

C, in-situ bundle

Production’s raw angles read 6–12 % shallow against the cosmic line, and fall with angle.

Cause: the bundle keeps the bench kernel but swaps the bench-fitted v for the 42.6 µm/ns prior. 42.6/36.6 ≈ 1.16 and 42.6/26.7 ≈ 1.60 are most of k_arm.

In-situ recipe: geometric v from free fits, robust kw per plane, seeder 3. A y flat at 1.00, A x within ±3 %.

~/scratch/ntof_insitu truth.parquet, reco_{prod_s3,is2_s3}_{A,C}.parquet, test split. Hover a point for σ_tan and n.

25

Details

Truth (ntof_cosmics/insitu_calib.py truth): 815 clean A–C crossings per arm from 14 run_149 sub-runs; a third trains the calibration, the rest is held out. The lever between chambers is 469 mm, so the joined line’s slope is known to ~0.002.

Bundles: production’s run_145 bundle (prod_s3, same seeder 3), and is2_A (production kernel, v 38.0, kw x 1.020 / y 0.993 from insitu_calib.py kwmed, a robust median over |tan| 0.15–0.45). is2_C: the r06 det7 kernel, v 28.7, kw x 1.001 / y 0.957. A least-squares kw (w0kw) is pulled by the tails and over-corrects A y by 7 %.

Ruled out as the cause, with bench M3 truth: S/N ÷ 8 (n_TOF S/N is 7–10× below bench), cropping to 20 samples, real n_TOF noise; and the template, ZS (off), the fit window, the w-scan range. A ref-pinned in-situ hyper fit is not the fix: its v = 39.2 is the χ²(v)-valley bias, so v comes from free fits against truth.

Chamber C’s 8–13 % core tails are not from the kernel; candidates are x/y noise, dead or hot strips, and an outward-going sign effect.

What this does not do: production then multiplies raw angles by the stage-3 capsule k (A 1.27), so production’s final angles read steep, not shallow. That k is the subject of the beam-scale slide.

The head-on loss was the seeder: 3 strips instead of 5 gives ×1.7 cosmic crossings, +45/52/40 % confirmed beam tracks

~/scratch/ntof_insitu seedtest_m{5,3}.parquet (σ: raw tan rescaled by its core median ratio) · seed_beam scint_confirmation.csv.

26

Details

At n_TOF signal-to-noise a near-normal track puts only 3–4 strips over threshold, and the beam seeder (MIN_STRIPS_BEAM = 5, set against single-strip junk) never seeds it; the bench seeder uses 3. Cosmic test (ntof_cosmics/seed_test.py): one-track A–C crossings 945 → 1570; below |tan| 0.08 the crossings that exist are badly measured at 5 strips and well measured at 3. Only |tan| < 0.02 stays poor.

Beam test (seed_beam_test.py, run_145 stat090_0000, all 7 tags, every trigger; report ntof_cosmics/results/seed_beam/report.html): confirmation = the track extrapolates to the SiPM-wall group that fired, minus the accidental rate from a shifted control. No particle is lost: of production tracks without a min-3 match, nearly all reappear with one view re-paired to another partner; only 22 (A) / 5 (C) vanish, in busy, junk-heavy events. Gained tracks are later and less often confirmed, so real but dirtier.

For same-chamber pairs: every two-track event is still ≥ 24 mm apart (median ~210 mm). The seeder neither makes close fake pairs nor recovers close pairs; it does re-pair 5–13 % of production tracks in busy events, which is T1’s x/y pairing problem. Validate both together.

The beam angle scale: the walls read the electrons’ scattering, and the cosmic scale stands

What multiplies production’s raw tan to give the true one, by four methods (left); why the beam walls disagree (right).

Cosmics read 1.15 at A’s wall, the A–C line’s 1.11; beam reads 0.89. In-beam muons read like beam-off ones. So the wall only disagrees for beam electrons.

Geant4, ideal reconstruction (the gap’s true line): what the same wall estimator reads, truth = 1

muons (1 GeV guns)

1.00

electrons > 4 MeV

0.92

electrons 2–4 MeV

0.63

all beam electrons

0.59

The gap is electron scattering between the gap and the wall, not the reconstruction. The wall (and the capsule k) are not angle truth for beam; the cosmic in-situ scale stands. Adopting it for beam is the next decision.

wall_edge_scale.csv (A) · scint-stack λ·k (C) · cosmic_wall_scale/summary.json · pooled k_true_by_borrowed_k.csv · kbeam_AC.txt · g4_angle/neutrons_wall_estimator.csv, single_summary.csv.

27

Details

Why this matters for pairs: an opening angle is only as good as the angle scale under it, and the stage-3 k (capsule pointing) multiplies every production angle. Until 7 Oct three truths disagreed for A: walls 0.89, cosmic A–C line 1.11, capsule 1.24–1.29.

Wall edges, beam (ntof_cosmics/wall_edge_scale.py, campaign, 31 runs, ~1 M single-track single-group events): where the fired wall group switches across a surveyed boundary, the median true tan at that strip position is known geometrically. The two outer boundaries give 0.893 with D_eff ≈ 330 mm, which refutes capsule pointing (234.6 mm). Sub-samples ruled out t0, partial tracks, fit quality and charge. By time after the flash: 0.77 at 10–15 ms, 0.91–0.93 after 20 ms.

Wall edges, cosmics (cosmic_wall_scale.py, run_149 put on the n_TOF clock): 3,088 x-plane tracks firing A’s wall read 1.15 (bootstrap 1.12–1.18), the A–C line’s value; the beam value is excluded. In-beam muons (inbeam_through_goers.py): A–C through-goers in beam runs read within 2–5 % of beam-off muons although their gain is ~1/3 lower, so gain, beam noise and space charge are not the cause.

Geant4 (ntof_cosmics/g4_angle/, condor 4402864/5): the data’s wall estimator applied to the gap’s true line. Muons read 1.00; capture electrons read 0.59 overall and 0.92 above 4 MeV. The wall sees where the electron arrives after scattering through the chamber and the material before the wall, not the direction it had in the gap. The data’s exact 0.89–0.92 is not yet reproduced: that needs a wft-digitised forward model of the Geant4 tracks and the ambient thermal-neutron population behind the late triggers, which no simulation has yet.

Consequence: never quote the wall scale or the capsule k_arm as beam angle truth. The cosmic in-situ scale (bundles is2_A, is2_C) is the calibration to adopt; that changes stage 3 / k_arm on the campaign and needs a decision. A related check: the ideal gap line itself reads electrons shallower than their emission (gap/gun 0.73 at 5 MeV), so the X17 opening-angle simulation must come from Geant4 hits, not truth directions.

28

Details

OCTOBER_2026.md §4 makes the campaign re-pass (O4) the single join point: it costs ~8–12 h of condor plus a day of chain, so it runs once, and everything that wants to ride it must be validated first. All the changes are opt-in; with every switch off the output is today’s production.

Shipping also needs plumbing that does not exist yet: bundles carrying the profc xy_pairing (wft_beam.make_bundle has no merge step for it), the switches and F in the condor environment, and a smoke gate that expects more tracks (today’s demands event counts identical to the August pass).

Source: sept26_prelim_analysis/SAME_CHAMBER_PAIRS.md, “The join”.

What this does not rule out

One sub-run, two chambers

run_145 stat090_0000, A and C. B and D are untested. All on the post-23-July (noisy) configuration.

Real triggers have no truth

split-ab bounds the cost of a threshold. The gain comes only from overlays of clean donors, and real pairs are busier.

Parallel co-located tracks

Degenerate at any Δt. They stay lost and must be carried as inefficiency.

The toy is one plane

Equal charges, tied t0, no second view: the x/y pairing loss is not in R1–R2.

Donor truth is a fit

A donor whose single-track fit is wrong gives a wrong label, and its twin inherits it.

Near normal, and B, D

The oracle and bench sit at tan ≈ 0.3; capsule pairs near the axis are near normal. Chambers B and D are untested.

Decisions

Next, in order

Cosmic wall test (beam vs cosmic scale) · T2 bundles · T1 bench and F ladder on them · one combined split-ab with seeder 3 · re-pass.

Ship or not

Bundles with profc pairing, the fixed-chain switches and F, seeder 3 and the rescue floor in the condor environment, then one re-pass.

Worth trying

A relative-tan dimension in the grid search (diverging pairs at 3–12 mm: 76 % vs ~97 % ideal); a near-normal oracle case; cosmic donors with true angles.

Flagged, outside this task

q_sum > 10⁶ on 12–33 % of stage-3 tracks from unconstrained depth bins: their charge-derived quantities are meaningless.

29

Details

The operating F is decided (A 1200, C 2400): one step lower fails the contract in both chambers. It was set on the v = 42.6 bundles and has to be re-derived once the in-situ bundles exist.

Handoffs: sept26_prelim_analysis/SAME_CHAMBER_PAIRS.md (the map, both branches), TWO_TRACK_LIMIT_RESUME.md (T1), ntof_cosmics/HANDOFF_TRACKING_2026-10-06.md §7–10 (T2). Full T1 record: TWO_TRACK_FIT_LOG.md. Long-form report with every table: ~/x17/sept26_prelim/two_track_limit/report/report.html.

Dropped, with reasons in the log: a fractional model error ε (no gain at a fixed false-split rate) and a looser 1.2 mm guard (it blocks 42 % of false splits on real singles).
